items.title: Jake Hanna interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997
items.q: Or Basie’d come in or Zoot would come in, I worked with Zoot or Red.

ctx.x: But then was there a jazz scene in L.A. that you could tap into at that time.

Well Donte’s was going then, and a lot of the guys worked that place for nothing you know. Twenty-five bucks a night, if you wanted cash. If you wanted to get a check you could get thirty-five but it probably wouldn’t, the check would probably bounce. That’s how silly it is you know. Joe Pass used to work, you know, the best guys. Red Norvo. But if Red was there you’d get money you know. Or Basie’d come in or Zoot would come in, I worked with Zoot or Red. But I hardly ever worked there with anyone else. Some of…
A couple of times the subject has come up about playing on top of the beat, playing behind the beat. Does such a thing exist?
